correctness.rationale: For all connected cubic bipartite twelve-vertex graphs, normalize to a 6x6 degree-three biadjacency matrix with first row 7 and sorted remaining rows. 147 connected matrices survive, and exhaustive isomorphism canonicalization yields precisely five types. For each type exact transition evaluation of all 4096 configurations proves F^4=F^2 and the stated first-entry/least-period and per-orbit basin histograms. Every class has positive t=2 populations. A separately implemented adjacency-list trajectory method agrees on all results, and the named prism/Franklin identities are checked by explicit graph isomorphism.

evidence: Kaaser–Mallmann-Trenn–Natale, arXiv:1508.03519v1, Definition 3 and Corollary 3.4: voting time bound 1 + number of edges - half the number of odd-degree vertices, equal to 13 for these graphs.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Both earlier theorems apply to more graphs, but general period-two recurrence does not control first-entry times, and the bound 13 is not the sharp bound 2. Neither result implies the five exact periodic and basin tables.

The broad general period-two theorem and general voting-time bounds lack the sharp two-update result and specific finite basin populations. A relevant prior five-graph census addresses paired domination, not majority dynamics. Relevant historical full-text and unindexed-result risks are acknowledged.

value.rationale: The full dynamical census of the complete natural five-class universe isolates graph-structural effects at fixed order and degree: while all classes have the same sharp two-update clock, their primitive two-cycle counts vary from 6 to 231 and their largest basin from 512 to 722. Two graphs sharing six squares have different attraction spectra, and the hexagonal prism and Franklin graph uniquely maximize different meaningful dynamical quantities. These are interpretable exact invariants over a natural complete classification, not a randomly chosen instance.
